#!/bin/bash
#FLUX -t 1h20m
#FLUX -N 2
#FLUX --tasks-per-node=16
#FLUX --exclusive
#FLUX -J parRay-team7
#FLUX --queue=cs
# The following PBS directive was found and ignored as it is not a Slurm directive:
# #PBS -S ./scripts/sing_shell.sh

echo `whoami`
## If not started with a scheduler, figure out where we are relative to the build directory
#####Snippet from:   http://stackoverflow.com/questions/59895/
SCRIPT_DIR="$( cd "$( dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" )" && pwd )"
#####end snippet
echo $SCRIPT_DIR
#IF FLUX_JOB_CWD is not set, we are not running in a job, choose directory relative to script.
FLUX_JOB_CWD=${FLUX_JOB_CWD:-${SCRIPT_DIR}/..}
echo $FLUX_JOB_CWD
#moves to the directory the user was in when they ran flux submit
cd ${FLUX_JOB_CWD} #assumed to be the source tree

#check that the script was submit from the right place.
if [ -d "./src" ]
then
	echo "We seem to be in the right place."
else
	echo "Not submit from the right place! Submit from the root of your repository."
	exit 1
fi

if [ -d "./build" ]
then
	rm -rf ./build
fi

SING_EXEC_LOCATION=${FLUX_JOB_CWD}/scripts/sing_exec.sh
SING_SH_LOCATION=${FLUX_JOB_CWD}/scripts/sing_shell.sh
BIN_DIR=${FLUX_JOB_CWD}/build/bin

#creates an out-of-tree build directory for CMake and moves to it
mkdir -p ${FLUX_JOB_CWD}/build
pushd ${FLUX_JOB_CWD}/build

echo "Compiling"
# The --mpi=pmi2 option from srun is not directly translated.
# flux run uses the MPI interface configured with the Flux instance, which is typically PMIx.
flux run -n 1 ${SING_EXEC_LOCATION} cmake ${FLUX_JOB_CWD}/src && \
flux run -n 1 ${SING_EXEC_LOCATION} make

echo "Run Tests"
flux run -n 1 ${SING_EXEC_LOCATION}  "${BIN_DIR}/bvh_test"
flux run -n 1 ${SING_EXEC_LOCATION}  "${BIN_DIR}/data_porting_test"



echo "Run Benchmarks"
#flux run -n 1 ~/scratch/sing_exec.sh  ./bin/bm_ray_tracing 
flux run -n 1 ${SING_EXEC_LOCATION}  "${BIN_DIR}/gen_random_scene 5"


for N_CPUS in 1 2 4 8 16 32 64
do

	#Individual MPI run
	echo "Doing MPI CPUS = ${N_CPUS} "
#	flux run --cpu-affinity=core -n ${N_CPUS} ~/scratch/sing_exec.sh ./bin/bm_mpi ./random_spheres_scene.data 2
	flux run --cpu-affinity=core -n ${N_CPUS} ${SING_EXEC_LOCATION} "${BIN_DIR}/bm_mpi ./random_spheres_scene.data 2"
done

reasons: The job requests a total of 32 tasks (2 nodes * 16 tasks-per-node).
The benchmark loop attempts to execute a `flux run` command with up to 64 tasks (`-n 64`).
This exceeds the total number of tasks allocated to the job, which will cause a runtime failure.
issues: A `flux run` command inside the benchmark loop has a potential quoting error: `${SING_EXEC_LOCATION} "${BIN_DIR}/bm_mpi ./random_spheres_scene.data 2"`. The executable and its arguments are quoted together as a single string, which will likely cause a 'file not found' error. The arguments should be separate from the executable path, for example: `${SING_EXEC_LOCATION} "${BIN_DIR}/bm_mpi" ./random_spheres_scene.data 2`.
The compilation steps (`cmake` and `make`) are run via `flux run -n 1`. While this works, it is unnecessary for serial commands and can be simplified by running them directly without `flux run`.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --time=01:20:00
#SBATCH --nodes=2
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=16
#SBATCH --exclusive
#SBATCH --job-name parRay-team7
#SBATCH -p cs
#PBS -S ./scripts/sing_shell.sh

echo `whoami`
## If not started with PBS, figure out where we are relative to the build directory
#####Snippet from:   http://stackoverflow.com/questions/59895/
SCRIPT_DIR="$( cd "$( dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" )" && pwd )"
#####end snippet
echo $SCRIPT_DIR
#IF SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR is not set, we are not running in PBS, choose directory relative to script.
SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR=${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR:-${SCRIPT_DIR}/..}
echo $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR
#moves to the directory the user was in when they ran qsub
cd ${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR} #assumed to be the source tree

#check that the script was submit from the right place.
if [ -d "./src" ]
then
	echo "We seem to be in the right place."
else
	echo "Not submit from the right place! Submit from the root of your repository."
	exit 1
fi

if [ -d "./build"]
then
	rm -rf ./build
fi

SING_EXEC_LOCATION=${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR}/scripts/sing_exec.sh
SING_SH_LOCATION=${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR}/scripts/sing_shell.sh
BIN_DIR=${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR}/build/bin

#creates an out-of-tree build directory for CMake and moves to it
mkdir -p ${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR}/build
pushd ${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR}/build

echo "Compiling"
srun --mpi=pmi2 --ntasks 1 ${SING_EXEC_LOCATION} cmake ${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR}/src && \
srun --mpi=pmi2 --ntasks 1 ${SING_EXEC_LOCATION} make

echo "Run Tests"
srun --mpi=pmi2 --ntasks 1 ${SING_EXEC_LOCATION}  "${BIN_DIR}/bvh_test"
srun --mpi=pmi2 --ntasks 1 ${SING_EXEC_LOCATION}  "${BIN_DIR}/data_porting_test"



echo "Run Benchmarks"
#srun --mpi=pmi2 --ntasks 1 ~/scratch/sing_exec.sh  ./bin/bm_ray_tracing 
srun --mpi=pmi2 --ntasks 1 ${SING_EXEC_LOCATION}  "${BIN_DIR}/gen_random_scene 5"


for N_CPUS in 1 2 4 8 16 32 64
do

	#Individual MPI run
	echo "Doing MPI CPUS = ${N_CPUS} "
#	srun --mpi=pmi2 --ntasks-per-node ${SLURM_NTASKS_PER_NODE} --cpu-bind=cores --ntasks ${N_CPUS} ~/scratch/sing_exec.sh ./bin/bm_mpi ./random_spheres_scene.data 2
	srun --mpi=pmi2 --cpu-bind=cores --ntasks ${N_CPUS} ${SING_EXEC_LOCATION} "${BIN_DIR}/bm_mpi ./random_spheres_scene.data 2"
done
